title: What is known about 1RB1LC_1LA0RE_0LD---_1LB1LD_1RB1RF_0LA0RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LC_1LA0RE_0LD---_1LB1LD_1RB1RF_0LA0RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Sweeps back and forth over a period-11 background (01010111101 and its rightward form 10101010010) with a soup of (01)^k, 1^3, 1^4 pieces; the clean zone at the left end grows; a halt needs B or F to read 0 just right of 1 1. Lean proves the sweep rules over the background words and the only local pattern that leads to a halt; no halt in 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 55,876 cells have been visited and 30,389 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.518). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503).

claims.title: The sweeps cross the background words whole
claims.text: 12 shift rules: for every n and every surrounding tape, a sweep in the stated state crosses n copies of a background word and leaves n copies of its partner, in the stated number of steps (for example L E> (01010111101)^n R ⟶ L (10101010010)^n E> R).

claims.title: The only way to a halt
claims.text: The machine halts only when C reads a 1, and the only ways there are B or F reading a 0 with 1 1 just left of it (B writes 1 or F writes 0, steps left, A reads the first 1 and steps left again, and C meets the second 1.

claims.title: What the tape looks like
claims.text: At the left end there is a clean zone of the period-11 word ((10100101010)91 at the right end of a sweep after 4·106 steps) that grows; the rest of the tape is a soup of (01)k with k = 4, 7, 10, 13, runs 13 0 14 and short copies of the period-11 word.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. In 10<sup>9</sup> steps B read a 0 with a 1 on its left about 4.2·10<sup>7</sup> times, and every time the cell before that 1 was a 0; nothing known rules out a second 1 there.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. Sweeps back and forth over a period-11 background (01010111101 and its rightward form 10101010010) with a soup of (01)^k, 1^3, 1^4 pieces; the clean zone at the left end grows; a halt needs B or F to read 0 just right of 1 1. This page runs the real machine, explains its sweeps and the words they rewrite, and lists what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 55,876 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
Crossing the background words, proved for every length.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.518). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.503).
After 109 steps the tape spans 55,876 cells (26,378 left of the start, 13,678 right), with a density of 1s of 0.544.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Sweeps that rewrite a periodic tape
html: Rightward, B and E (with F) cross the period-11 word whole: E turns 01010111101 into 10101010010, B turns 10101111010 into 01010100101; they also swap 01 and 10 and turn 11101 into 10010. Leftward, A, B, C and D take the rightward forms back (37 steps per copy), and C crosses 10 unchanged.

At the left end there is a clean zone of the period-11 word ((10100101010)91 at the right end of a sweep after 4·106 steps) that grows; the rest of the tape is a soup of (01)k with k = 4, 7, 10, 13, runs 13 0 14 and short copies of the period-11 word.

sections.heading: What one sweep does to the words it crosses
html: A shift rule says that a sweep crosses any number n of copies of a word in one state and leaves n copies of another word behind. These are proved in Lean for every n and every tape around them (lean/Rules.lean); S> is the head in state S on the next cell, L and R the rest of the tape.

sections.heading: The one pattern that halts, and why it has not appeared
html: The machine halts only when C reads a 1, and Lean proves that the only ways there are B or F reading a 0 with 1 1 just left of it (B writes 1 or F writes 0, steps left, A reads the first 1 and steps left again, and C meets the second 1; halt_needs_pattern, lean/Halt.lean).
In 109 steps B read a 0 with a 1 on its left about 4.2·107 times, and every time the cell before that 1 was a 0; nothing known rules out a second 1 there.
Next step. Describe the soup as blocks of (01)k and find what one round trip does to k.

summary: Sweeps back and forth over a period-11 background (01010111101 and its rightward form 10101010010) with a soup of (01)^k, 1^3, 1^4 pieces; the clean zone at the left end grows; a halt needs B or F to read 0 just right of 1 1.
